scholarships.title: France Excellence Europa Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: Campus France (French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs)

existing.description: The France Excellence Europa scholarship programme, developed by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and managed by Campus France, lets students from 26 EU Member States study at Master's level at a French higher education institution. It pays a semi-annual maintenance allowance of EUR 6,850 and a one-off installation allowance of EUR 1,700, exempts holders from administrative registration fees for a national degree in public institutions and from the CVEC, and arranges social protection and complementary health insurance. The award lasts up to 12 months for a Master 2 enrolment and up to 24 months for a Master 1 enrolment, and applications are sent electronically to the French Embassy in the applicant's country of nationality.
eligibility: National of one of the 26 eligible EU Member States: Germany, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Croatia, Denmark, Spain, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Czech Republic, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia or Sweden
Not a French national, including bi-nationals
At least 18 years old when the mobility period in France begins
Does not already possess a master's degree from any country (there is no upper age limit subject to this condition)
Admitted to a French higher education institution in Master 1 or Master 2
Not the holder of a French higher education degree and not currently registered in France for a higher education degree
Not the recipient of an Erasmus+, AUF or other French ministry scholarship
existing.eligibility_summary: National of one of 26 EU member states; at least 18 years old; admitted to a French higher education institution in Master's 1 or Master's 2; not holding a French higher education degree; not currently registered in France for a higher education degree; not receiving another French ministry/Erasmus+/AUF scholarship.
benefits: Exemption from registration fees for national diplomas
Priority assistance in finding CROUS university residences (rent paid by student)
Insurance enrollment during first three months
coverage: Exemption from registration fees for national diplomas

existing.best_fit: EU students seeking partial funding for Master's studies in France.
existing.notes: Does not cover course fees, international or national transportation. Applications pre-selected by French embassies, then evaluated by Ministry. 2025 was the inaugural call; 2026 call expected.
existing.duration: A maximum of 12 months when enrolling in Master 2 and a maximum of 24 months when enrolling in Master 1. The stay must begin between 1 September and 31 December of the year the scholarship is awarded, and no deferral is possible.
existing.deadline_display: Typically April annually (2025 deadline: 30 April 2025; 2026 call expected similar timeline)

scholarships.title: France Excellence Major Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: AEFE (Agency for French Education Abroad) / French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs

existing.description: France Excellence-Major is a French government scholarship run by AEFE for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs that supports the best non-French baccalaureat holders from the network of French schools abroad to continue their higher education in France. Around 800 foreign students are supported at any one time over five years of study, and about 200 new holders join each year. Applications require pre-selection by the head of the French school abroad and online entry on the dedicated Cascade application, followed by assessment by the French embassy's cultural cooperation service and a selection commission convened by AEFE each May. Selection weighs school results, a coherent orientation project, involvement in school life and extracurricular activity, and motivation for demanding French higher education. Holders receive a family-need-rated monthly allowance of EUR 280 or EUR 860, complementary health cover, and, at the higher rates, round-trip travel and CROUS housing.
eligibility: Enrolled in classe de terminale at a homologued French school abroad (lycee de l'enseignement francais a l'etranger)
Has an orientation project in French higher education in a programme awarding a diploma recognised by the State
Wishes to commit to demanding studies from the baccalaureat
Submits orientation wishes on the Parcoursup portal or via specific institutional procedures, identical to those in the scholarship application
Shows genuine motivation and capacity to adapt to life in France
Is pre-selected by the proviseur or proviseure of the French school abroad
For definitive award: obtains the baccalaureat with a 'tres bien' mention and confirms enrolment in the announced track
existing.eligibility_summary: Non-French national; enrolled in terminale (final year) in an approved French international school abroad (homologated by AEFE); excellent academic results; plan to pursue higher education in France; obtain baccalaureate with mention 'très bien'.
benefits: Three levels of grant based on family situation (amounts vary annually)
Status of French government scholarship holder (facilitates visa, residence permit, university housing)
Follow-up and support by AEFE throughout studies
coverage: Three levels of grant based on family situation (amounts vary annually)
Status of French government scholarship holder (facilitates visa, residence permit, university housing)
Follow-up and support by AEFE throughout studies
documents: Online application via Cascade application (preselected by school head)
Letter of admission/plans for higher education in France
application_method: Online via Cascade application (preselection by homologated French international school abroad)
existing.best_fit: Top non-French students in terminale at French international schools abroad seeking funding for higher education in France.
existing.notes: Approximately 200 new scholars per year; supports up to 5 years of study in France. Distinct from Eiffel (which is for Master's/PhD already admitted to French institutions).
existing.duration: Five years of study in France, referenced by AEFE to the time needed to obtain a Master 2 or equivalent; about 800 foreign students are supported at any time, with around 200 new holders joining each year.
existing.deadline_display: Typically February-March annually (2026 campaign: 16 February - 12 March 2026)
existing.program_type: Government scholarship of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, awarded by AEFE and managed financially by Campus France
